data.title: Test Double
data.tagline: A test double is a controllable object that replaces a real dependency during testing.
data.learningOutcome: You can tell when to isolate an uncontrolled dependency and when a real-service connection still needs verification.
data.description: When an order module requests payment, a double can reliably return success, rejection, or timeout so tests verify how the page handles each. Mock, stub, fake, and spy can be different kinds of test double; not every double is simply a Mock, and it cannot prove a real service is connected.

learning.assumes: You know a page or module may depend on payment, email, or a third-party API.
learning.outcome: You can tell when to isolate an uncontrolled dependency and when a real-service connection still needs verification.

distinctions.label: Test data and Fixture
distinctions.explanation: A Test Double replaces the behavior of a real dependency with something controllable. A Test Data and Fixture prepares and cleans up the data and environment a test needs.

explanation.title: Turn hard-to-arrange outcomes into stable input
explanation.text: A real payment service may not reliably produce rejection or timeout on demand. A double returns a specified result for a case, making error display, retry, and logging repeatable.

explanation.title: Match the double to the boundary under test
explanation.text: A double suits testing an order module’s response to rejection; verifying protocol and authentication with the real provider still needs a controlled real connection.

data.boundary: A test double is not a simulated production service and not another word for every Mock. It replaces one dependency only during tests; it proves how the unit handles preset outcomes, not that the real dependency is currently healthy.

lessonPractice.title: You need to verify that a rejected payment shows a retry entry, but the real payment sandbox is sometimes unavailable. What is best?

options.label: Have a payment test double consistently return rejection, then assert the page shows retry
options.feedback: Correct. The test asks how the page handles rejection, and the double makes that prerequisite repeatable.

options.label: Wait until the real payment service happens to reject
options.feedback: The prerequisite is uncontrolled, slow, unstable, and hard to repeat.

options.label: If the double passes, declare real payment integration verified
options.feedback: A double does not prove real service connection, authentication, or protocol works.

data.agentPrompt: Add a test double that consistently returns payment rejection and verify the page shows a clickable retry entry. Keep one controlled-environment real payment connection check as well; do not substitute the double result for it.
